note: Authored by reading Tafsir al-Tabari in English against the reader's modern translation. Each phrase carries the app's own words for that piece of the verse, a plain modern English line of my own, the Arabic of the piece, and the numbered paragraphs of the commentary that speak of it.

phrases.translation: By the sky full of constellations
phrases.text: God swears by the heaven with its constellations. The commentators differed: some said the constellations are the stars, some that they are towers, some that they are castles in the sky, and some that the heaven holds sand and water. Tabari takes the dwellings of the sun and moon.

phrases.translation: and the promised Day ˹of Judgment˺
phrases.text: And He swears by the day He has promised His servants, the day of the resurrection, on which judgment is passed between them. The Prophet said: the promised day is the day of resurrection.

phrases.translation: and the witness and what is witnessed
phrases.text: And He swears by the witness and the witnessed. The commentators put forward many pairings, most often Friday as the witness and the day of Arafah as the witnessed, others the human being and the day of resurrection, and others the Prophet and Friday. Tabari leaves it open, for God did not say which he meant.

phrases.translation: Condemned are the makers of the ditch—
phrases.text: Cursed are the people of the trench, and the trench is the pit dug in the earth. The commentators differed over who they were: some said a believing people who were offered a choice between the fire and giving up their faith, and some said the unbelievers who persecuted them. Tabari takes the latter.

phrases.translation: the fire ˹pit˺, filled with fuel—
phrases.text: The fire, supplied with fuel, that is, with thick and steady firewood. The fire stands in the genitive because it is inside the trench, as though it were the same as the trench.

phrases.translation: when they sat around it
phrases.text: When these people of the trench were sitting by the fire, that is, at the edge of the pit. The words say upon it, but the meaning is the bank of the trench.

phrases.translation: watching what they had ˹ordered to be˺ done to the believers
phrases.text: And they were present, as witnesses, to what they did to the believers.
phrases.ar: وَهُمۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَفۡعَلُونَ بِٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ شُهُودٞ

phrases.translation: who they resented for no reason other than belief in Allah—the Almighty, the Praiseworthy—
phrases.text: They found nothing blameworthy in the believers, and did nothing to them for any reason except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, severe in His punishment of those He punishes, the Praiseworthy, praised for His kindness to His creatures.
phrases.ar: وَمَا نَقَمُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ إِلَّآ أَن يُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡحَمِيدِ

phrases.translation: ˹the One˺ to Whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and earth. And Allah is a Witness over all things
phrases.text: He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And God is witness over the deed of these people against the believers, and over the rest of their deeds and the deeds of all His creation, and He will requite them.
phrases.ar: ٱلَّذِي لَهُۥ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ شَهِيدٌ

phrases.translation: Those who persecute the believing men and women and then do not repent will certainly suffer the punishment of Hell and the torment of burning
phrases.text: Those who tortured the believing men and believing women, and did not repent, will have the punishment of Hell in the hereafter and the punishment of the burning in this world. The commentators say the torture was the burning with fire.
phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ فَتَنُواْ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ ثُمَّ لَمۡ يَتُوبُواْ فَلَهُمۡ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابُ ٱلۡحَرِيقِ

phrases.translation: Surely those who believe and do good will have Gardens under which rivers flow. That is the greatest triumph
phrases.text: Those who believed in the oneness of God and did good deeds have gardens in the hereafter with rivers flowing beneath them, and wine and milk and honey. That is the great victory, the reward of all their striving.
phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَهُمۡ جَنَّٰتٞ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡكَبِيرُ

phrases.translation: Indeed, the ˹crushing˺ grip of your Lord is severe
phrases.text: The grip of your Lord, O Muhammad, against anyone He seizes is severe. And this is a warning that He may send down on this people the same chastisement that came on the people of the trench.

phrases.translation: ˹For˺ He is certainly the One Who originates and resurrects ˹all˺
phrases.text: He is the one who begins and repeats. The commentators differed: some say it is the creation that He begins and then repeats on the day of resurrection, and some say the punishment. Tabari takes the punishment, because God speaks of His grip and His severity.

phrases.translation: And He is the All-Forgiving, All-Loving—
phrases.text: He is the One who forgives whoever turns to Him in repentance, and the One who loves him. The commentators say He is the Beloved and the Merciful.

phrases.translation: Lord of the Throne, the All-Glorious
phrases.text: Lord of the noble throne. The reciters differ on whether the last word is read as describing God or the throne, and Tabari says both readings are well known and the reciter is right either way.

phrases.translation: Doer of whatever He wills
phrases.text: He does whatever He wills. He is abundant in forgiveness toward the one who repents, and He punishes the one who persists in his sins. Nothing stops Him from a deed He wills to do.

phrases.translation: Has the story of the ˹destroyed˺ forces reached you ˹O Prophet˺—
phrases.text: Has the account of the hosts reached you, O Muhammad, of those who ranged themselves against God and His messenger with their tormenting? It has, so bear patiently the harm your people do you, as God's messengers did, and do not let it stop you from delivering the message.

phrases.translation: ˹the forces of˺ Pharaoh and Thamûd
phrases.text: Pharaoh and Thamud. God names Pharaoh alone because he commanded the army, and Pharaoh stands in the genitive as a nearer explanation of the hosts.

phrases.translation: Yet the disbelievers ˹still˺ persist in denial
phrases.text: It is not that these people have heard nothing of the peoples before them and of the punishment that came down on them for denying the messengers. They keep on denying God's revelation out of their own preference for their desires and their following of the ways of their forefathers.

phrases.translation: But Allah encompasses them from all sides
phrases.text: God surrounds their deeds from behind, counting them, with nothing of it hidden from Him, and He will requite them for all of it.

phrases.translation: In fact, this is a glorious Quran
phrases.text: Nay, it is a noble Qur'an, said in answer to those who claimed the Qur'an was poetry and rhymed prose.

phrases.translation: ˹recorded˺ in a Preserved Tablet
phrases.text: Recorded on a well-preserved tablet, guarded against any addition to it or any taking away from it. The reciters differ on whether the last word describes the tablet or the Qur'an, and Tabari says both readings are correct in meaning.
